contract: state/board-session.json, as bin/fm-session-start.sh publishes it at every locked session start (bin/fm-session-start.sh's header is the contract's owner). Each case gives the environment the session start ran in and the Claude session-registry entry the harness wrote for this session; expect is the record they must produce, or null when the identity must be refused and no record written. source names which route produced the session id: environment when the session stated it in CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID, registry when it was read back out of the registry under the session lock's harness pid. The environment route is open only while CLAUDE_PID is absent or names a running process. Absent says nothing, because older builds do not export it, and the record then carries the lock's harness pid. Present but non-numeric or dead is evidence the whole environment was inherited from some other session, so CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID is ignored with it and only the registry route under the lock pid remains: that start publishes the lock pid's own live entry or nothing at all, never the environment's id. {{PID}} stands for the live harness pid, substituted by both sides before comparing. registered_at is asserted for presence and ISO-8601 UTC shape only, never for a value. Entries here carry no procStart or pidDomain, whose liveness rule is exercised against real processes in tests/fm-board-session.test.sh rather than pinned as data, and the dead-CLAUDE_PID half of the environment rule is exercised there for the same reason.
peer_implementation: logbook's board wake path, which reads this record and selects the session with bridge-axi agent-wake --session. Recorded 2026-09-07, while that side is being built against this file; no case has a divergence to record yet.

cases.name: registry-route-derived-name
cases.note: the fallback route, and the ordinary session it was written for: nobody named it, so the name carries a random byte redrawn on every start and is informational only.

cases.name: registry-route-user-named
cases.note: a person ran claude --name or /rename. The name would have been a valid selector, and the record still carries the session id, so the reader never has to decide.

cases.name: registry-route-name-set-through-the-environment
cases.note: CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_NAME writes the name and omits nameSource entirely. name_source is null, and null must not be read as 'nobody named it' - this name is as stable as a user one.

cases.name: registry-route-no-name-and-no-cwd
cases.note: every informational field is optional and absent becomes null, never an empty string. The session id alone is what a wake needs.

cases.name: registry-route-non-interactive-kind-is-recorded-not-filtered
cases.note: kind is reported as the registry states it. Firstmate publishes the session that holds the lock whatever its class; whether to wake a non-interactive one is the reader's call, and it can only make it if the value survives.

cases.name: registry-route-no-session-id
cases.note: the session id is the selector the record exists to carry, so an entry without one, and no environment to fall back from, is refused outright rather than published as a record a reader cannot act on.

cases.name: registry-route-session-id-outside-the-selector-charset
cases.note: a session id carrying anything but letters, digits, dot, dash or underscore is refused. It would be interpolated into this record and then into a wake selector, so it is validated rather than escaped.

cases.name: registry-route-informational-field-this-reader-cannot-represent
cases.note: a cwd holding a quote is read back truncated by the narrow field reader, so the whole entry is refused rather than published as malformed JSON.

cases.name: environment-route
cases.note: the preferred route: inside a tool call the session states its own id, so there is no lookup to miss. The registry entry for the pid the harness names still supplies the informational fields.

cases.name: environment-route-without-a-named-process
cases.note: CLAUDE_PID absent says nothing, since older builds do not export it, so the environment route stays open on CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID alone and the pid is the harness pid the session lock holds; its entry still supplies the informational fields. The opposite case, a CLAUDE_PID that is present but names no running process, marks the whole environment as inherited from some other session and closes the route; it needs a real dead process, so it is exercised in tests/fm-board-session.test.sh.

cases.name: environment-route-with-no-registry-entry
cases.note: the environment names the session, and there is no entry to enrich it from. The record is still published, because the session id is what a wake needs and the rest is informational.

cases.name: environment-route-disagreeing-with-a-live-entry
cases.note: the live entry under this pid is that process's own record, not a corpse, so naming a different session is drift between two vendor sources rather than staleness. Neither is trusted over the other: nothing is written, because an unregistered session is a board that keeps polling, where a wrong session id is a wake sent confidently into nothing.

cases.name: environment-session-id-outside-the-selector-charset-falls-back
cases.note: an unusable environment id is not fatal: the registry route still answers, and the record says so. The same charset rule applies whichever route offered the value.
